inspection_summary.note: Texas HHSC inspections, report investigations and assessments since October 2017, updated daily.

occurrences.finding: Documented Annual Training- Required Content: Five staff files reviewed did not have the health and safety trainings required on:   Emergency preparedness, Preventing and controlling the spread of communicable diseases, Administering medication, Preventing and responding to emergencies due to food or an allergic reaction, Understanding building and physical premises safety, Handling, storing, and disposing of hazardous.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documented Annual Training- Required Content (26 TAC §746.1309(e))

occurrences.finding: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Pre-Service Training: Three staff did not  have pre-service training.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Pre-Service Training (26 TAC §746.1301(a)(2)(A))

occurrences.finding: Required Personnel Records: Five out of twelve staff files reviewed during inspection were missing the documents on personal record information, and annual training to include transportation and medication training. Two of the files were missing a copy of the driver's license and proof of education. Three files were missing the pre-employment affidavit.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Personnel Records (26 TAC §746.901)

occurrences.finding: Safety Requirements for Cribs - Sanitize Each Crib: One crib had lots of debrie and stains on  the crib sheet. The  plexiglass was smeared. The other crib had  paper rolls, and a balled up crib sheet. Pictures were taken of these findings.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety Requirements for Cribs - Sanitize Each Crib (26 TAC §746.2409(b))

occurrences.finding: Diaper Changing Equipment - Smooth, Non-absorbent, Easy to Clean Surface: Two diaper changing stations in the toddler classrooms  had debrie  all around the inside of the table and under the mat. Pictures were taken.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Diaper Changing Equipment - Smooth, Non-absorbent, Easy to Clean Surface (26 TAC §746.3503(a))

occurrences.finding: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment: The floor in the boy's restroom was not clean during the investigation inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know children responsible for: A caregiver did not know which children they were responsible for when they left a child on the playground with a different group of children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know children responsible for (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(1))

occurrences.finding: Required Health Statement - Written, dated within past year, indicates child is physically able to participate in operation's child-care program: One out of five children enrollment forms reviewed  was missing the health statement.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Health Statement - Written, dated within past year, indicates child is physically able to participate in operation's child-care program (26 TAC §746.611(a)(1))

occurrences.finding: Diaper Changing Equipment - Smooth, Non-absorbent, Easy to Clean Surface: The diaper changing mat in the toddler classroom was torn along one side of the  seam.     Corrected when the diaper changing mat was removed from the diaper changing table.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Diaper Changing Equipment - Smooth, Non-absorbent, Easy to Clean Surface (26 TAC §746.3503(a))

occurrences.finding: Required Admission Information - Physician Information: One out five children enrollment forms reviewed during the visit  was missing information on the emergency medical attention section.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Admission Information - Physician Information (26 TAC §746.605(10))

occurrences.finding: Required Admission Information - Emergency Contact: One out of five children enrollment forms  reviewed during inspection was missing the emergency contacts.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Admission Information - Emergency Contact (26 TAC §746.605(6))

occurrences.finding: Requirements during probation: The operation has failed to maintain the child-caregiver ratio logs for the month of October and November.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Requirements during probation (26 TAC §745.8641)

occurrences.finding: Health Statement on File within 1 Week of Admission: Four out of ten children files were missing the health statement information.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Health Statement on File within 1 Week of Admission (26 TAC §746.611(b))

occurrences.finding: Documented Annual Training Area - 24 Hours Required: One caregiver did not accumulate the required trainings with certificates for the year 2024-2025 period.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documented Annual Training Area - 24 Hours Required (26 TAC §746.1309(a))

occurrences.finding: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking.: One caregiver had an expired CPR/1st aid certification since November 2024.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking. (26 TAC §746.1315(a))

occurrences.finding: Requirements during probation: The operation failed to follow the probation condition on ratios when several of the classrooms were out of ratio on a visit conducted by CCR on 9/9/2025 for inspection 4074769.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Requirements during probation (26 TAC §745.8641)

occurrences.finding: Documented Annual Training- Required Content: Five out of  twelve staff files were reviewed. Two of the  caregiver files were missing trainings on handling, storing, and disposing of hazardous materials ,understanding building and physical premises safety, preventing and responding to emergencies, administering medication, preventing and controlling the spread of communicable diseases, and emergency preparedness.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documented Annual Training- Required Content (26 TAC §746.1309(e))

occurrences.finding: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children: A caregiver providing care to seven children, ages four months to twenty- one months was over ratio by three children, and the assistant director providing care to twenty-seven children ages two to five years old was over ratio by sixteen children.     Note: This was corrected at inspection when a second caregiver was placed in both classrooms.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children (26 TAC §746.1601)

occurrences.finding: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards: There was a hard plastic pipe sticking out of the mulch on the preschool/school age playground.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards (26 TAC §746.3701)

occurrences.finding: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment: Several air vents had accumulated dust.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)

occurrences.finding: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days: Three infant feeding instructions were not updated.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days (26 TAC §746.2421(b))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Interact positively with children: Based on the evidence gathered in the investigation conducted, it can be determined that a caregiver did not use positive interactions when they pulled a four year old child up by the arm and carried the same child by the arms to the other side of the classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Interact positively with children (26 TAC §746.1203(5))

occurrences.finding: Children Not Required to Sleep - May Not Force Child to Sleep: Based on the evidence gathered in the investigation conducted, it can be determined that a blanket was placed over a child's head by a caregiver while the child laid on the cot during naptime.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children Not Required to Sleep - May Not Force Child to Sleep (26 TAC §746.2905(1))

occurrences.finding: Provide care consistent with child's habits, interests, strengths, special needs, including any special supervision needs: Based on the evidence gathered in the investigation conducted, it can be determined that a pre-k classroom was not in control as majority of the children refused to nap and played on and around the cots.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Supervision of Children (26 TAC §746.1203(4))

occurrences.finding: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children: Based on the evidence gathered in the investigation conducted, it can be determined that the pre-k classroom was out of ratio as there were twenty children to one caregiver with majority of the children were awake and were not asleep or laying down on their cots. As majority of the children were awake the ratio of one caregiver to 15 three year olds or one caregiver to 18 four year olds must be followed.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children (26 TAC §746.1601)

occurrences.finding: Director Responsibilities - Employee Assignments: Based on the evidence gathered in the investigation conducted, it can be determined that a caregiver was assigned to a classroom that did not math their skills and abilities as the classroom was not in control.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director Responsibilities - Employee Assignments (26 TAC §746.1003(3))

occurrences.finding: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Brief Supervised Separation: Based on the evidence gathered in the investigation conducted, it can be determined that a four year old was separated for thirteen minutes.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Brief Supervised Separation (26 TAC §746.2803(4)(D))

occurrences.finding: HRC42.054 - Required Fees: Fees have not been paid.
occurrences.violation_type_title: HRC42.054 - Required Fees (26 TAC §HRC42.054 - Required Fees)

occurrences.finding: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Pediatric First Aid with Rescue Breathing: One out of the ten staff files reviewed during inspection did not have Pediatric First aid and CPR training.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Pediatric First Aid with Rescue Breathing (26 TAC §746.1301(a)(3)(A))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: Based on the investigation conducted, it can be determined that a caregiver did not exercise good judgement by failing to notify management of a child stating their arm hurt following a fall on the playground the caregiver again did not notify anyone when the child complained of arm pain again hours later.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Maintenance Procedures for Active Play - Keep Records for 3 Months: Playground maintenance inspections and repair records  were not available for review during inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance Procedures for Active Play - Keep Records for 3 Months (26 TAC §746.4751(d))

occurrences.finding: Complying with Laws and Rules: The operation was not adhering to the requirements of the Plan of Action that was agreed upon between Child Care Regulation and the operation.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Complying with Laws and Rules (26 TAC §746.201(9))

occurrences.finding: Installation and Maintenance of Loose-fill Surfacing - Six Inches if Equipment 5 Ft or Less: Loose fill observed by the slides on the playground did not meet the required 6 inches of dept.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Installation and Maintenance of Loose-fill Surfacing - Six Inches if Equipment 5 Ft or Less (26 TAC §746.4907(a)(1))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know number of children responsible for: Caregivers in the infant and preschool classrooms gave incorrect number of children they supervised.  The infant class caregiver said she had nine infant, when she only had eight.  The preschool class caregiver had 22 when she said she had 23.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know number of children responsible for (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children: The caregiver in the twos classroom was observed caring for twelve two year old children.  NOTE: This was corrected when the director called parents to pick up their children.  A preschool classroom caregiver was observed supervising twenty two three year old children by herself.    NOTE:  This was corrected as the director arrived and assigned the cook/caregiver to assist in that classroom. As the cook stepped away to finish lunch preparation, the director stepped in to supervise.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children (26 TAC §746.1601)

occurrences.finding: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days: 6 infants did not have updated feeding schedules.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days (26 TAC §746.2421(b))

occurrences.finding: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk: During a DFPS investigation, it was determined that a situation that placed a child at risk was not reported to Child Care Regulation.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.305(a)(6))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: During the course of a DFPS investigation, it was determined that the director did not use good judgment when she allowed a two year old child who had been left behind in an infant room, to stay in the infant room for 20 minutes.  This disrupted the routine for the two year old child as well as the infants in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know children responsible for: During a DFPS investigation, it was determined that a caregiver did not know which children she was responsible for which resulted in a child being left behind in another classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know children responsible for (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(1))

occurrences.finding: Infant Care Area - Not Used as a Passageway: The infant classroom was used as a passageway for a two year old class to return to their own assigned classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Infant Care Area - Not Used as a Passageway (26 TAC §746.2403(6))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: During the course of a DFPS investigation it was determined that a child was left alone, in a bathroom.  Pictures were also received showing 4 toddler age children standing on tables.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment: A clogged toilet was not repaired attracting bugs in the children's restroom creating unsanitary conditions.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: Certain caregivers did not exercise good judgment when purposely not notifying management of a broken toilet at the operation.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Cots, Beds, Mats Labeled With Child's Name: Two classrooms did have a number/child assignment map for the cots observed used by the children in care.      Note: This was corrected at inspection when the map was created.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Cots, Beds, Mats Labeled With Child's Name (26 TAC §746.4503(b))

occurrences.finding: Written Operational Policies - Instructions for Contacting Licensing Office/Online and TX Abuse & Neglect Hotline: The operation's policies did not inlcude  the instructions on how a parent may contact the local Licensing office, access the Texas Abuse and Neglect Hotline, and access the HHSC website.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Operational Policies - Procedures parents access minimum standards online, TX A/N hotline, and HHSC website (26 TAC §746.501(a)(23))

occurrences.finding: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children: Sprays containing sanitizing liquids were observed in an unlocked cabinet in the pre-k building accessible to the children in care.     Note: This was corrected at inspection as the sprays were removed and placed out of reach during the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children (26 TAC §746.3407(12))

occurrences.finding: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Pediatric First Aid with Rescue Breathing: Three out of the three staff files reviewed during inspection did not inlucde a copy of their first aid and CPR.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Pediatric First Aid with Rescue Breathing (26 TAC §746.1301(a)(3)(A))

occurrences.finding: Required Personnel Records: Staff trainings were not available for review during inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Personnel Records (26 TAC §746.901)

occurrences.finding: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Pediatric First Aid with Rescue Breathing: One out of the two files did not have current first aid and CPR training.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Pediatric First Aid with Rescue Breathing (26 TAC §746.1301(a)(3)(A))

occurrences.finding: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children: During the follow up inspection the first classroom had 30 children to 1 teacher and at 9:30 the director moved children to another classroom. In the infant room there were 8 infants 2 months to 11months and 2 children that were 1 year and 10 months and 1 year and 8 months and 2 teachers.    Corrected at inspection the director separate the preschool children form the pre-k children and removed the 2 toddlers from the infant room.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children (26 TAC §746.1601)

occurrences.finding: Director Responsibilities - Operate in Compliance: The director failure to comply with minimum standards when she allowed multiple classrooms out of ratio and placing child safety at risk.    Corrected at inspection 2 more employess came in to work in the classrooms and the asst. director came to work. So the director was able to come out of the classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director Responsibilities - Operate in Compliance (26 TAC §746.1003(1))

occurrences.finding: Children Handwashing After Outdoor Activities: They preschool children returned into the classroom from outside play and went straight to the table and started playing with toys. The children nor the teacher washed there hands.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children Handwashing After Outdoor Activities (26 TAC §746.3417(4))

occurrences.finding: Director Responsibilities - Operate in Compliance: The director is did not ensure the center is meeting minimum standards and maintaining the ratio.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director Responsibilities - Operate in Compliance (26 TAC §746.1003(1))

occurrences.finding: Caregiver Responsible for Each Child: The teachers in the pre-k and toddler classrooms are out of ratio during morning routine.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Caregiver Responsible for Each Child (26 TAC §746.1501(b))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling: The teachers were yelling at the children to shut up and be quiet, and sit down with a harsh tone in the toddler and preschool classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling (26 TAC §746.2805(5))

occurrences.finding: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children: The after school classroom was observed over ratio by four children in care.    NOTE:  This was corrected at inspection, when the inspector notified the office manager who had completed the bus runs to assist in the after school classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children (26 TAC §746.1601)

occurrences.finding: Director's Absence -  Employees Know Who Is in Charge: During inspection, while the director, assistant director, and office manager were out to lunch, the caregivers supervising children during naptime, did not know who was left in charge, nor for how long.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director's Absence -  Employees Know Who Is in Charge (26 TAC §746.1013(c))

occurrences.finding: Required Personnel Records - Required Affidavit: Re cited-Four of the four employees still have not had an employment affidavit added to their employment file.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Personnel Records - Required Affidavit (Form 2985) (26 TAC §746.901(4))

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Immunizations: One of the three children's immunization records remain to be submitted.  One of the two children's healthcare statements remain to be submitted.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Immunizations (26 TAC §746.603(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation: An employee was working in the toddler classroom with no background check.      This was corrected during inspection when that employee was sent home and advised could not return until it is returned cleared.    Director submitted background check while inspector in office.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation (26 TAC §745.641)

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Withholding Active Play: During the investigation it has been determined that the caregiver withholds active play from children as a result of bad behavior.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Withholding Active Play (26 TAC §746.2805(9))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling: During this investigation, it has been found that caregivers do yell at the children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling (26 TAC §746.2805(6))

occurrences.finding: Required Personnel Records- Meets Requirements: The director has been unable to obtain employee documents as required.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Personnel Records- Meets Requirements (26 TAC §746.901(2))

occurrences.finding: Documentation of Drills: The fire drill list did not show fire drills conducted for last two months.  The smoke/carbon monoxide detectors and fire extinguishers  do not reflect checks for the past 5 months.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documentation of Drills (26 TAC §746.5205(4))

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Immunizations: The director has not received documents from parents for children's records.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Immunizations (26 TAC §746.603(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Immunizations: Three of ten child records reviewed did not contain  immunization records    Two of ten files did not have required health care physician statements.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Immunizations (26 TAC §746.603(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Required Personnel Records- Meets Requirements: Two of eight staff files did not have verification of employment qualifications.    Four of eight files did not have employment affidavits.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Personnel Records- Meets Requirements (26 TAC §746.901(2))

occurrences.finding: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Playground Maintenance Records: The operation did not have current, up to date documentation for  playground maintenance checks.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Playground Maintenance Records (26 TAC §746.801(8))

occurrences.finding: Required Personnel Records- Meets Requirements: Two of eight staff files did not have verification of employment qualifications.    Four of eight files did not have employment affidavits.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Personnel Records- Meets Requirements (26 TAC §746.901(2))

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Immunizations: Three of ten child records reviewed did not contain  immunization records    Two of ten files did not have required health care physician statements.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Immunizations (26 TAC §746.603(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months
occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months (26 TAC §746.5101(a))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: During the investigation, it has been determined that the staff did not display good judgment and self control while children were in care when a caregiver confronted another caregiver resulting in a verbal altercation in front of children in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Maintenance Procedures for Active Play - Monthly Maintenance Checklist: The center could not produce a previously completed playground checklist.    Corrected at inspection: The checklist was completed during the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance Procedures for Active Play - Monthly Maintenance Checklist (26 TAC §746.4751(b))

occurrences.finding: Arrangement of Napping Equipment - Provides Access to Walkway: The classrooms had cots that were put to close together and the children would need to cross over other children to get out.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Arrangement of Napping Equipment - Provides Access to Walkway (26 TAC §746.2909(4))

occurrences.finding: Annual Sanitation Inspection: The health inspection was last conducted on 05/10/2021 and another inspection has not been conducted since then.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Sanitation Inspection (26 TAC §746.3401(a))

occurrences.finding: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric CPR: Four out of six staff records reviewed did not have proof of a valid CPR training.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric CPR (26 TAC §746.1315(b))

occurrences.finding: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking.: Four out of six personnel staff records reviewed did not have proof of a valid First Aid training.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking. (26 TAC §746.1315(a))

occurrences.finding: Posting Requirements - Letter or form from the most recent Licensing Inspection or Investigation: The previous inspection posted was from 2020.    Corrected at inspection: The new inspection form was printed and posted.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Posting Requirements - Letter or form from the most recent Licensing Inspection or Investigation (26 TAC §746.401(2))

occurrences.finding: Safety Requirements for Active Play Equipment - No Pinch, Crush, or Shear Points: Two tricycles observed in the playground had broken seats that had shear points.     Corrected at inspection: The tricycles were removed from the playground.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety Requirements for Active Play Equipment - No Pinch, Crush, or Shear Points (26 TAC §746.4601(7))
